{{Short description|81st season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=August 2014}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = National Hurling League 2012 |image = |dates = 25 February – 6 May 2012 |teams = 34 |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = [[Eoin Larkin]] |manager1 = [[Brian Cody]] |titles = 15th |team2 = Cork |captain2 = [[Patrick Horgan]] |manager2 = [[Jimmy Barry-Murphy]] |oneb = Clare |twoa = Carlow |twob = Kildare |threea = Fingal |threeb = Fermanagh |previous = [[2011 National Hurling League|2011]] |next = [[2013 National Hurling League|2013]] }} The '''2012 [[National Hurling League]]''' commenced in February 2012. 34 [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]] county hurling teams: 32 from [[Ireland]] (including [[Fingal hurling team|Fingal]] but not [[Cavan GAA|Cavan]]), [[London GAA|London]] and Warwickshire, contested it. On 6 May [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] defeated [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final to win their 15th NHL title, moving them to second place in the all-time roll of honour, behind [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] who have won 19 Leagues.{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/kilkennys-early-blitz-ends-rebel-resistance-3101757.html|title=Kilkenny's early blitz ends Rebel resistance|date=7 May 2012|work=Irish Independent|access-date=15 May 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/2012/0508/1224315743718.html|title=Just another test passed for in-form Larkin and Kilkenny|date=7 May 2012|work=Irish Times|access-date=15 May 2012}}{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0506/319847-allianz-hurling-final-cork-v-kilkenny/|title=As it Happened: Cork 0-16 Kilkenny 3-21|date=7 May 2012|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=15 May 2012}} ==Format== The 2012 format was originally to consist of five divisions: Divisions 1 and 2 having eight teams in each, Division 3A six, Division 3B seven, and six teams in Division 4. However, this was controversially altered to a system of six divisions, with six teams in divisions 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B and 3A, and four in division 3B.{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/counties-to-vote-on-new-hurling-league-format-2845335.html|title=Counties to vote on new hurling league format|date=11 August 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 March 2012}} This meant that many counties were effectively relegated to a lower division.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/1012/hurling_league.html |title=Hurling League changes are announced |date=12 October 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=6 March 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120121053858/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/1012/hurling_league.html |archive-date=21 January 2012 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/revamp-announced-for-next-years-hurling-league-517286.html|title=Revamp announced for next year's hurling league|date=20 August 2011|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 March 2012}} It was agreed in October 2011 that there would no longer be an eight-team Division 1, with the top division hurling counties giving their approval to the new system.{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/martin-breheny-hurlings-elitist-divide-2907096.html|title=Hurling's elitist divide|date=15 October 2011|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 March 2012}} The league settings are as follows: *'''Division 1A:''' Top three teams qualify for NHL semi-finals. Bottom two teams play a relegation playoff, with the losing team relegated. *'''Division 1B:''' Top two teams play division final, with the winner being promoted and qualifying for NHL semi-final. Bottom two teams play a relegation playoff, with the losing team relegated. *'''Division 2A:''' Top two teams play division final, with the winner being promoted. Bottom two teams play a relegation playoff, with the losing team relegated. *'''Division 2B:''' Top two teams play division final, with the winner being promoted. No relegation. *'''Division 3A:''' Top two teams play division final, but the winner is not promoted.
